c.tagline: White-sand beaches and cool dunes on Rio's Região dos Lagos.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis are metered; ride-hailing apps like Uber and 99 are usually cheaper than street taxis, especially in summer high season.

emergency.note: 190 reaches the military police, 192 summons a SAMU ambulance, and 193 reaches the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Keep clear of the hillside favela areas such as Jacare away from the beachfront, particularly at night.
Phone snatching and theft of unattended beach belongings happen along Praia do Forte; keep valuables minimal after sunset.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Cabo Frio around the Boulevard Canal and Nossa Senhora da Assunção church, near the 17th-century São Mateus Fort and the São Bento canal; best for first-timers wanting shops, restaurants and services within walking distance.
The city's main beach, a long stretch of famously cool white sand backed by hotels, kiosks and restaurants; the liveliest and most convenient base for beachgoers.
A canal-side neighbourhood along the Itajuru channel lined with seafood restaurants, bars and boat moorings; good for waterfront dining and nightlife a short hop from the beaches.
A busy commercial district known for the Rua dos Biquínis (Bikini Street) beachwear market and shopping, close to Praia do Forte; suits travellers who want retail and easy beach access.
A quieter residential beach area to the north with the long Praia do Peró and protected sand dunes; suits families and travellers wanting calmer sands and nature.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water, as visitors do throughout Brazil.

transit.hours: Municipal buses run roughly 05:00 to around midnight, thinning out late at night; taxis and ride apps fill the gap.
transit.note: Cabo Frio has no metro or tram; getting around relies on municipal buses, taxis and ride-hailing apps, plus a very walkable beachfront and canal district.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver (or with the regional RioCard where accepted); there is no citywide smartcard.

bus: Intercity coaches to Rio de Janeiro, Búzios and the Região dos Lagos (Auto Viação 1001, Salineira, Montes Brancos)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually already added to restaurant bills; extra tipping is optional.

food.name: Acai na tigela
food.desc: Frozen acai pulp whipped thick and topped with banana and granola; on Cabo Frio beaches it is eaten as a mid-afternoon cool-down, not a dessert.

food.name: Tapioca
food.desc: Cassava-starch crepe cooked on a hot griddle and folded over cheese, coconut or condensed milk; the standard Brazilian beach breakfast and late snack.

food.name: Caipirinha
food.desc: Cachaca muddled with lime and sugar over ice; on the Costa do Sol it is often made with passion fruit or local cashew instead of lime.

food.desc: Chilled green coconut water drunk straight from the machete-opened nut, the default Brazilian beach hydration and cheaper than bottled water.

landmarks: Praia do Forte
Cabo Frio's showpiece beach unfurls powdery white 'moon dust' sand and improbably turquoise water for four kilometers, framed by the historic seaside fortress.
Forte São Mateus
A weathered 17th-century Portuguese fort built to fend off pirates, its cannon-studded ramparts guard the end of Praia do Forte with sweeping ocean views.
Ilha do Japonês
A tiny islet in the Itajuru channel ringed by shallow, gin-clear lagoon waters, reachable by kayak or a short swim, perfect for lazy sandbar afternoons.
Praia das Conchas
Sheltered by rocky headlands and cacti-dotted hills, this crescent cove's calm emerald waters and rustic beach barracas feel like a secret slice of Caribbean.
Praia do Peró
Seven kilometers of dune-backed white sand beloved by surfers and kitesurfers, its wild, undeveloped stretches contrast beautifully with Cabo Frio's busier city beaches.
Dunas do Peró (Dama Branca Dunes)
Shifting white sand dunes rise like a miniature desert behind Peró beach, where sandboarders carve slopes and sunset walks reveal a lunar landscape.
Boulevard Canal (Canal do Itajuru)
Cabo Frio's lively waterfront promenade traces the boat-filled Itajuru channel past seafood restaurants, moored schooners, and pastel facades glowing at golden hour.
Convento Nossa Senhora dos Anjos
This whitewashed 1696 Franciscan convent on a hilltop houses a religious art museum and offers one of the loveliest colonial silhouettes on Brazil's Lakes Region coast.
Praia das Dunas
A broad, breezy continuation of the Forte shoreline backed by protected dunes, favored by families and beach-sport lovers seeking space away from the crowds.
Mirante do Pontal do Atalaia (Arraial do Cabo)
A short drive away, this clifftop viewpoint above Prainhas do Pontal reveals twin turquoise coves so vivid they're nicknamed the Brazilian Caribbean.

train.note: No railway serves the Região dos Lagos, and Brazil has no intercity passenger trains. Arrive by coach from Rio de Janeiro or by car on the RJ-124 motorway.

bus.note: No international coaches. Auto Viação 1001 (https://www.autoviacao1001.com.br/) runs very frequent buses from Rio de Janeiro's Rodoviária Novo Rio to Cabo Frio in about 2h30, continuing to Búzios and Arraial do Cabo; book through ClickBus (https://www.clickbus.com.br/). Local buses and vans link the three towns every few minutes.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Cabo Frio. Boats from the canal and from neighbouring Arraial do Cabo run snorkelling and island trips around the Ilha do Farol and Praia do Forno, which are excursions sold by the hour or day rather than transport.

half.name: Búzios
half.blurb: Glamorous former fishing village turned beach resort, with a string of coves loved by celebrities since the 1960s.

half.name: Arraial do Cabo
half.blurb: Fishing town known as Brazil's Caribbean, with turquoise water and boat trips out to Ilha do Farol.
